doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: World's greatest bass player
summary: A tap dancer introduces him as the world's greatest bass player, and he reflects that there is no such thing.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well I would say that it’s great, wonderful. And it’s still amazing. It seems to be getting bigger and bigger. It doesn’t end. And all I did was, at the time when I was looking for employment I was trying to survive. And I’ll tell you one thing. This thing about becoming the world’s greatest bass player. One night I was on stage with Barney Briggs — Bunny.

And then we were playing and he was dancing, and then he went up to the mic and he says, “ladies and gentlemen, I’d like to introduce you to the world’s greatest bass player.” I said to myself I made it. Isn’t that something?
Just one person said that. And I said I made it. Yeah.
Of course you and I realize there is no such thing, everybody has a way of expressing themselves, it’s just different. And it depends on personal taste. A note is a note.
